hints: Find the $x^1$ and $x^2$ terms in the binomial expansion of $(2+\frac{1}{2}x)^5$.
Identify the combinations when multiplying $(1-2x)(2+\frac{1}{2}x)^5$ that produce $x^2$: $(x^2 \text{ term}) \times 1$ and $(x^1 \text{ term}) \times (-2x)$.
Calculate $20(1) + 40(-2)$ to obtain the final coefficient.
walkthrough:
Determine the relevant terms in the expansion of $(2+\frac{1}{2}x)^5$ using the binomial theorem:
$$\text{Term in } x: \quad \binom{5}{1}(2)^4\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)^1 = 5 \times 16 \times \frac{1}{2}x = 40x$$
$$\text{Term in } x^2: \quad \binom{5}{2}(2)^3\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)^2 = 10 \times 8 \times \frac{1}{4}x^2 = 20x^2$$

Identify the terms giving $x^2$ when multiplied by $(1-2x)$:
$$\text{From } (20x^2)(1) = 20x^2$$
$$\text{From } (40x)(-2x) = -80x^2$$

Sum the components to determine the total coefficient of $x^2$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^2 = 20 - 80 = -60$$

ai_rubric.Finding Coefficients in Expansions: Finds $x$ term $40x$ and $x^2$ term $20x^2$ in $(2+\frac{1}{2}x)^5$ (B1, B1). Multiplies appropriately by $(1-2x)$ using $20(1) - 40(2)$ (M1). Obtains $-60$ (A1).
